paragraphs: On Saturday, Pat and May went to the market with their dad. The market was full of people, and Pat wanted to taste everything. "Please stop, Pat," said May, but he only laughed. Pat ate three sweet cakes and a big bag of candy. He drank two bottles of cold orange juice too. That night he was very tired, and he did not brush his teeth. On Monday at lunch, Pat held his mouth with one hand. Pat did not eat his rice, and he did not talk. May took him to the nurse's room.

"Good afternoon, Pat," said Nurse Jill. "What is the problem?" "My tooth hurts," said Pat. Nurse Jill sat down beside him and took a notebook. "Which tooth is it?" asked Nurse Jill. "This one, at the bottom on the left," said Pat. "When did the pain start?" "Yesterday after dinner," said Pat.

"Does it hurt all the time?" asked Nurse Jill. "No, only when I drink something cold," said Pat. "Are you able to eat and sleep?" "I am able to sleep, but I cannot eat hard food," said Pat. "Do you eat a lot of sweet things?" "No, not many," said Pat. May looked at him and said nothing. "Do you brush your teeth every night?" "Almost every night," said Pat, and he looked at his shoes.

Nurse Jill washed her hands first. "Open your mouth wide, please," she said. She looked inside with a small light. "I can see a small dark spot on this tooth." "Why does it hurt in my head?" asked Pat. "The tooth tells your brain, 'I need help,'" said Nurse Jill. Pat touched his head and laughed a little.

She wrote a note for the dentist and a note for Pat's mom. "I will make an appointment with the dentist," said Nurse Jill. "Here is my advice for today." "Drink water, do not eat sweet things, and brush your teeth in the morning and at night." "Can I do exercise in PE?" asked Pat. "Yes, exercise is good for your health," said Nurse Jill. "Your teeth must last all your life," said Nurse Jill. "I was born with no teeth," said Pat. "We all were," said Nurse Jill with a smile. "That is why you must take care of the teeth that you have." May opened the door. "I will check your teeth every night," she said.
text.summary: Pat eats many sweet things at the market and does not brush his teeth. On Monday his tooth hurts, and he tells Nurse Jill about it. She gives advice and makes an appointment with the dentist.

sentences.text: On Saturday, Pat and May went to the market with their dad.
The market was full of people, and Pat wanted to taste everything.
"Please stop, Pat," said May, but he only laughed.
Pat ate three sweet cakes and a big bag of candy.
He drank two bottles of cold orange juice too.
That night he was very tired, and he did not brush his teeth.
On Monday at lunch, Pat held his mouth with one hand.
Pat did not eat his rice, and he did not talk.
May took him to the nurse's room.
"Good afternoon, Pat," said Nurse Jill.
"What is the problem?"
"My tooth hurts," said Pat.
Nurse Jill sat down beside him and took a notebook.
"Which tooth is it?" asked Nurse Jill.
"This one, at the bottom on the left," said Pat.
"When did the pain start?"
"Yesterday after dinner," said Pat.
"Does it hurt all the time?" asked Nurse Jill.
"No, only when I drink something cold," said Pat.
"Are you able to eat and sleep?"
"I am able to sleep, but I cannot eat hard food," said Pat.
"Do you eat a lot of sweet things?"
"No, not many," said Pat.
May looked at him and said nothing.
"Do you brush your teeth every night?"
"Almost every night," said Pat, and he looked at his shoes.
Nurse Jill washed her hands first.
"Open your mouth wide, please," she said.
She looked inside with a small light.
"I can see a small dark spot on this tooth."
"Why does it hurt in my head?" asked Pat.
"The tooth tells your brain, 'I need help,'" said Nurse Jill.
Pat touched his head and laughed a little.
She wrote a note for the dentist and a note for Pat's mom.
"I will make an appointment with the dentist," said Nurse Jill.
"Here is my advice for today."
"Drink water, do not eat sweet things, and brush your teeth in the morning and at night."
"Can I do exercise in PE?" asked Pat.
"Yes, exercise is good for your health," said Nurse Jill.
"Your teeth must last all your life," said Nurse Jill.
"I was born with no teeth," said Pat.
"We all were," said Nurse Jill with a smile.
"That is why you must take care of the teeth that you have."
May opened the door.
"I will check your teeth every night," she said.
